title: REST vs gRPC vs WebSocket vs SSE
description: Choose a protocol from retry safety, duplex need, and the commit boundary. Encoding is not a ledger.

cells.workload: Public and partner APIs, browser and mobile JSON, resource-shaped reads and keyed writes. TokenX POST /debits and Ad Click POST /clicks.
cells.consistency: Each request is its own contract. GET may be cached. POST is not idempotent without a body key. HTTP 200 is a statement about a response, not proof unless the handler waited on the commit.
cells.latency: JSON encode/decode plus HTTP/1.1 or HTTP/2. Debuggable. Compression trades CPU for WAN bytes.
cells.scaling: Stateless handlers. Cacheable GET at CDN/edge. Writes scale with the store, not with the courier brand.
cells.failure: Client timeout is UNKNOWN if the handler might have committed. Gateway retry of unkeyed POST duplicates effects. 409 on a unique key is stored success, not a ban.
cells.costOps: OpenAPI, additive field evolution, gateway auth and rate limit. Easy to inspect on the wire.
cells.whenNot: Duplex chatter (typing, shared cursors) or a fleet that already speaks protobuf stubs and needs per-RPC deadlines as default. Never put spendable GET balances on a shared CDN.

cells.workload: Internal unary and streaming RPCs, protobuf schemas, deadlines, service-to-service. Same TokenX handler as JSON when you transcode.
cells.consistency: Unary is still one RPC. Deadlines cancel the caller, not the ledger. Stub retries without transfer_id mint a second command. Not a commit protocol. Streaming frames are not money.
cells.latency: Compact codec and HTTP/2 (or HTTP/3) multiplexing. Wins only if you do not JSON-transcode at the edge. TCP loss still HOL-blocks HTTP/2 streams.
cells.scaling: Many RPCs on one connection. Server streaming for feeds of derived events. Does not replace a partitioned log.
cells.failure: UNAVAILABLE plus automatic retries. Proto tag reuse breaks old binaries. Transcoding bugs are a second parser.
cells.costOps: Codegen, proto compatibility, grpc-web or a JSON gateway for browsers. You operate deadlines and retry budgets in stub + mesh + app.
cells.whenNot: Public JSON-only clients with no stub story, or a claim that binary encoding makes retries safe. TokenX unkeyed unary retries are the same bug as REST.

cells.workload: Duplex notifications, typing, presence, operator consoles that send frames. TokenX receipts after the ledger commit; not the debit itself.
cells.consistency: Frames are transport. Presence is last_seen plus TTL, not authorization. Resume tokens ({connection_epoch, last_seq}) address a derived buffer. Missed seq means fetch status from the API.
cells.latency: After upgrade, low per-frame cost. Reconnect gap is a buffer, not a rollback. Handshake still pays TCP/TLS unless you already had a warm connection.
cells.scaling: Concurrent sockets, sticky L7 or a connection-aware router, ping QPS. Fan-out amplification is a separate budget. Slow consumers need a bound, then disconnect or coalesce.
cells.failure: Deploy drain and proxy idle timeouts RST live sockets. Unbounded send buffers are a memory incident. Partition shows presence ghosts until TTL.
cells.costOps: Connection-aware load balancing, drain, resume buffers, backpressure. Sticky affinity still breaks on restart.
cells.whenNot: TokenX debit as a WS message type without the same (tenant, transfer_id) as HTTP. Presence as a spendable lock. Billed Ad Click ingest on a socket ACK.

cells.workload: Server-to-client event streams: Ad Click operator dashboards, one-way TokenX notifications, last-event-id resume. Client need not send frames.
cells.consistency: Last-Event-ID resumes a derived stream. Dashboards are labeled-stale views of the billed log. Not duplex, not a ledger, not read-your-writes unless you wait on the source.
cells.latency: HTTP response stream. First byte after commit+outbox lag. Proxies that buffer turn a stream into one dump.
cells.scaling: One direction, often cheaper than WebSocket if the client is silent. Still one handler occupancy per waiter unless the runtime is event-loop idle-friendly.
cells.failure: Intermediary buffering, dropped connections, resume gaps. Same drain story as other long HTTP. Fail-open dashboards must label delay; they must not ACK billed clicks.
cells.costOps: Fewer moving parts than WebSocket (no ping protocol of your own if the client uses EventSource). You still own Last-Event-ID buffers and proxy config.
cells.whenNot: The client must send frames (use WebSocket) or you need a request/response commit (use REST/gRPC). Do not CDN-cache the event stream as a shared GET of money.

assumptions: Protocols are contracts. TokenX POST/unary commits only after the ledger unique insert; Ad Click 2xx only after unique log append. Timeouts are UNKNOWN.
gRPC here is HTTP/2 or HTTP/3 plus protobuf and deadlines. It is not automatically faster than JSON and does not provide end-to-end once-only effects.
WebSocket and SSE are notification paths. Presence and resume buffers are derived and expire. Sticky L7 is transport, not fencing.
TCP HOL, QUIC, and 0-RTT replay sit in the connection-lifecycle lesson. TLS 0-RTT is forbidden for TokenX debits.
Latency figures are order-of-magnitude interview planning numbers, not SLOs from a named production fleet.
